attempts.label: DANDI:001749
attempts.paper_title: Padilla-Coreano, N., Batra, K., Patarino, M. et al. (2022). Cortical ensembles orchestrate social competition through hypothalamic outputs. Nature 603, 667-671.
attempts.entry_title: Social competition behaviour in the mPFC recording cohort (Padilla-Coreano et al. 2022)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Padilla-Coreano, Batra, Patarino et al. (2022) on dandiset 001749, which holds the wireless mPFC recordings of 20 mice in 53 reward competitions, with tone times, port entries, AlphaTracker poses and the nine hand-scored behaviour labels. It checks the files' clocks and units against the paper and tests the behavioural findings of Extended Data Fig. 5 (competitions won by rank, rewards, latency, port occupancy, pushing success and time displaced) and the HMM-GLM decoding of behaviour from multi-unit activity (Figure 1i, ED Fig. 5j-k), with the paper's HMM-GLM code ported from MATLAB, on the files whose neural offset can be placed. The single-unit findings cannot be tested, as the files do not mark the paper's curated cells.

outcomes.statement: A 6-state HMM-GLM decodes the 9 behaviour labels from mPFC multi-unit activity above chance and better than a GLM or an ensemble of 9 GLMs, while the GLM and the 9 GLMs do not differ.
outcomes.quote: An HMM-GLM model with 6 hidden states decoded behavioral labels from neural activity with superior cross-validated performance to static models

statistics.about: HMM-GLM, 9 GLMs and GLM against chance
HMM-GLM with leave-one-animal-out cross-validation against chance

outcomes.notes: On the 512 trials of the 17 files used (10 mice), the 6-state HMM-GLM AUCs with the one-bin shift are 0.60 to 0.83 (median 0.774), all 9 above 0.5 (sign test p = 0.0039), above the GLM (median 0.541, rank-sum p = 0.0003) and the 9 GLMs (median 0.539, p = 0.0003); GLM against 9 GLMs p = 0.627. Without the shift the HMM-GLM median is 0.713 and p = 0.0009 against each. Crossings in either direction give the same outcome (median 0.910). Random folds pass with the shift (p = 0.047) and fail without it (p = 0.233). Without 20191029-chrimson2-2-2v3 (482 trials, 16 files, 9 mice) every test passes (median 0.693, p = 0.0003 against each static model, GLM against 9 GLMs p = 0.627). Rates z-scored per channel fail at the code's learning rate of 1e-6 (median 0.475 and 0 of 9 above 0.5 with one seed, median 0.511 and 7 of 9 with another), and the paper's own input z-scored gives chance at that rate too (median 0.494); at 1e-4 z-scored rates decode all 9 labels here (median 0.576, p = 0.0039) and on the paper's input (median 0.650). Leave-one-mouse-out (10 mice) gives 9 of 9 above 0.5 (p = 0.0039). On the paper's own processed input the ported code gives HMM-GLM AUCs 0.79 to 0.98 against static medians near 0.59 and meets every test. The measured values are the trials, files and mice analysed, outside the tolerances of the expected 965, 32 and 13; the labelled files hold 965 trials, 34 files and 14 mice (within tolerance if a session is a file), and the paper's input holds 14 animals too. The SVM is not run and the Kruskal-Wallis across five models is not judged.
deviations: 17 of the 34 labelled files (512 of 965 trials, 10 of 14 mice), those whose recording can be placed on the behaviour clock (clear port-entry offset, within 10 s of the other clear files of that day and cage, scaled spikes matching the recording, labels matching the port entries at r >= 0.3); the offset is in no file. One of the 17 (20191029-chrimson2-2-2v3, 30 trials) peaks 8 s away from its port-entry offset against the paper's processed input; leaving it out changes no test.

Input computed from the raw ElectricalSeries as Methods 17 describe it ("applying a common reference average and determining spikes using 4 standard deviations from the mean"; 70 time stamps of 200 ms), with the 600 to 6,000 Hz band of Methods 11; mean and SD per channel over each 14 s trial window (the span is not given; a standard choice).

HMM-GLM as fixed by run_model.m and model_HMMGLM.m (github.com/Tyelab/HMMGLM at 3fc3567), ported line by line to Python (hmmglm.py); its numerical guards are kept, and NaN scores are ignored in the AUC as perfcurve does by default.

Readings of the criterion run one at a time against the main one (negative crossings, counts, AUC with the shift, contiguous folds in session order). They differ in outcome (z-scored rates fail; random folds fail without the shift), so the outcome rests on counts and contiguous folds, which the paper's processed input (uint16 counts per bin) and run_model.m (contiguous blocks) support. An assumption. The z-scored failure is at the code's learning rate, set for counts; z-scored rates decode at a learning rate of 1e-4, which the code does not use.
Static decoders fitted by maximum likelihood (L-BFGS) with a ridge of 1e-4 on inputs scaled by the training SD; the paper names no solver or regularisation.
Folds in which a label is absent give no AUC for it and are left out of its mean over folds (2 folds for resist).

outcomes.statement: Held-out log-likelihood of the HMM-GLM increases with the number of hidden states and plateaus at 6 states.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 5j, left; Methods 17, Cross-validation and Model Selection
outcomes.quote: We found that as you increase the number of hidden states, the log likelihood increases, reaching a plateau at the 6-state model
outcomes.notes: Held-out log-likelihood per trial (mean over 10 folds, SEM) on the input of fig1i-hmmglm-decodes-behaviour is -154.8 for 1 state, -124.5 (4.4) for 2, then falls slowly to -126.1 (4.3) at 6 and -126.9 (4.2) at 10. Reading (a) selects 2 and reading (b) selects 2. With crossings in either direction the mean is highest at 4 states (-121.3, SEM 3.8) and the smallest number within one SEM of it is 3, so no reading selects 5, 6 or 7. On the paper's input, run for 1 to 10 states, the values rise from -529.6 at 1 state to -126.5 (SEM 0.57) at 6 and are lower at every larger number (-127.6 at 10); both readings select 6. The port selects 6 on the paper's input and not on the input computed from the dandiset, so the difference comes from the input, not from the code.
deviations: Input, files and code as in fig1i-hmmglm-decodes-behaviour (17 of 34 labelled files, 512 trials).
States 1 to 10, as the criterion reads them; each with its own seed.

outcomes.statement: The 6-state HMM-GLM predicts behaviour above chance whichever relative rank group is used for training and for testing.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 5k; Results, mPFC neurons encode competition behavior
outcomes.quote: The model performed equally well when training for one relative rank and testing on the other

statistics.n: 9 behaviour labels, 482 dom and 478 sub trials

outcomes.notes: Trials of files of relative dominants (299, 7 mice) and subordinates (213, 4 mice). With crossings in either direction, the reading the outcome rests on, every combination passes, with and without the shift. Dom to sub and sub to dom give 9 of 9 AUCs above 0.5 (sign test p = 0.0039; medians 0.821 and 0.788, lowest AUC 0.780 and 0.582), and both 10-fold runs within a group give 9 of 9 (p = 0.0039). With negative crossings, dom to sub gives 8 of 9 (p = 0.039), sub to dom 7 of 9 (p = 0.18; AUCs 0.48 to 0.91), dom 10-fold and sub 10-fold 9 of 9 (p = 0.0039); without the shift sub to dom is again 7 of 9 (p = 0.18), so not every combination passes on that reading. With random folds the within-group runs give 9 of 9. On the paper's input (its own rank per trial, 487 dom and 478 sub trials, the counts of the 34 labelled files here) both directions and both within-group 10-fold runs give 9 of 9 (p = 0.0039).
deviations: Input, files and code as in fig1i-hmmglm-decodes-behaviour, except the threshold direction; 512 of the 965 trials (legend 482 dom and 478 sub).
The sub group holds 4 mice (213 trials), so training on it rests on few animals.

The outcome rests on the threshold reading. It takes crossings in either direction of mean plus or minus 4 SD; Methods 17 says only "determining spikes using 4 standard deviations from the mean". The two readings give different outcomes, and this one is better supported by the paper's processed input. Matched trial by trial, the paper's counts are 1.06 times the crossings in either direction (median over the 17 files, range 0.63 to 1.41) and 1.47 times the negative crossings (1.21 to 2.11, never below 1), and its median rate per channel (28.15 Hz) is nearer that of crossings in either direction (23.05 Hz) than of negative crossings (16.41 Hz). The choice was made after the result was seen, and the counts computed here follow the paper's poorly in time under both readings, so the count level does not settle the direction. An assumption.

This claim rests on crossings in either direction, while fig1i-hmmglm-decodes-behaviour and ed5j-six-states keep negative crossings as their main reading; each has the same outcome under both readings, so no outcome depends on the difference.

outcomes.statement: In the recording cohort, rank 1 mice won the highest percentage of competitions.
outcomes.quote: Percent competitions won by absolute rank is highest for rank 1 mice in dataset used for mPFC recordings
outcomes.notes: Competitions per own rank over the 53 files are 12, 11, 15 and 15, all within tolerance of 12, 12, 15 and 14. Of the 36 competitions whose outcome the labels give (34 from the file's own labels, 2 from the competitor's), rank 1 won 10 of 11 (90.9%), rank 2 1 of 8 (12.5%), rank 3 4 of 9 (44.4%) and rank 4 5 of 8 (62.5%). There are no ties, so both readings agree, and the variants of the trial rule (delivery at 0.49 s, switch as both mice in the window) give the same table; the switch variant cannot differ, as labels change only on whole seconds. 17 competitions have no labels.
deviations: 36 of the 53 competitions could be decided; the 10 ephys files and 7 mPFC-LH files have no labels, of their own or of their competitor.

Trial winners come from the hand-scored labels with the rule of the Methods (Reward competition behavioral analysis); the occupant over 1.5 to 3 s is the mouse with more in-port bins, and a switch is a window whose first and last occupied bins belong to different mice. The other switch reading gives the same outcomes.

Reward delivery is taken at 2 s after tone onset from Methods 5 ("A 10uL reward of vanilla Ensure was delivered 2 seconds after tone onset"); the files give 0.49 s, run as a variant with the same result.

outcomes.statement: Among mice wearing loggers, relative dominants and subordinates obtained similar numbers of rewards, while the body weight difference between competitors correlated with rewards won.
outcomes.quote: number of rewards obtained by relative dominants ( dom ) and subordinates ( sub ) during the reward competitions between animals wearing loggers

statistics.about: percent body weight difference against rewards won

outcomes.notes: Rewards (trials won) did not differ by the paired t-test. Over 20 sessions (main) dominants won 14.35 and subordinates 12.15 (mean difference 2.20, 95% CI -4.04 to 8.44, p = 0.498); over the 34 labelled files 14.12 and 12.38 (p = 0.505); with delivery at 0.49 s, p = 0.543. The second part of the claim, the correlation of body weight difference with rewards won, could not be tested; no file holds a body weight (the subject record has age, genotype, sex, species, strain, subject id and description, and no description gives a weight). The rewards part holds and the other is untested.
deviations: The body weight correlation is not tested (data missing).
Pairs are 20 sessions (main) or 34 files, against the paper's 22 pairs; the files count the two files of 14 sessions as separate pairs, though they are two views of one session.
Trial winners as in ed5b-rank1-wins-most, from the Methods passage cited there.

outcomes.statement: In win trials, relative subordinates had longer latencies to pick up the reward than relative dominants.
outcomes.quote: Subordinates had longer latencies to pick up the reward during win trials
outcomes.notes: With each label trial set against the tone of the same index, subordinates enter the port later in their win trials (median 1.47 against 1.01 s, 189 and 211 trials, rank-sum p = 0.0196, KS p = 0.0036; next entry for a mouse already in the port, p = 0.0204). With each file's best tone shift p = 0.0458 over all files; without the files whose labels and port entries agree at r below a cut-off, p is 0.0623, 0.375, 0.375 and 0.0662 at cut-offs of 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 (at 0.3, 1.48 against 1.38 s, 166 and 185 trials; KS p = 0.067). Without the shift, keeping only the files that agree at the same index, p is 0.0206 at 0.2, 0.158 at 0.3 (1.40 against 1.28 s, 158 and 171 trials), 0.0211 at 0.4 and 0.0022 at 0.5 (17 files, 140 and 115 trials); this reading drops the files whose label trials start at a later tone. From the hand-scored labels, which need no alignment, p = 0.206 over all win trials and 0.16 over the trials of the main test; over mouse means p = 0.055 (entries) and 0.059 (labels). Subordinates are slower in every reading. With each file's tones placed by its best shift the rank-sum is below 0.05 only when the files whose labels and entries disagree are kept (cut-offs 0 and 0.1); on the files aligned without a shift it is below 0.05 at every cut-off except 0.3, so the outcome rests on the choice of reading.
deviations: Win trials and their port entries are aligned through the labels; in 18 labelled files the labels hold fewer trials than tones and in several the label trials start at a later tone, which no file records. The outcome takes the reading that sets aside trials whose labels cannot be placed on the port entries (best tone shift, files at r >= 0.3); an assumption, since the paper does not say how its latencies were matched to trials. The best shift is taken over the tone index because it places the files whose label trials start at a later tone, which the reading without a shift drops. The cut-off of 0.3 is a choice; with the best shift every cut-off from 0.2 to 0.5 gives p above 0.05.
400 win trials with port entries in the main reading (351 in the outcome's reading), against the paper's 326 dom and 358 sub trials.
How a mouse already at the port at onset is counted is not given; both readings (0, or its next entry) are shown and agree.
The legend's one-way RM-ANOVA is not judged, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: Percent port occupancy during the tone did not differ by relative rank in the recording cohort.
outcomes.quote: Percent port occupancy during tone across relative rank (n=31 sessions, paired t-test p=.90)
outcomes.notes: Percent of the 10 s tone labelled in the port did not differ by relative rank; dominants 26.37% and subordinates 20.23% over 20 sessions (main; mean difference 6.14, 95% CI -4.79 to 17.08, paired t-test p = 0.284), 25.19% and 20.72% over 34 files (p = 0.327).
deviations: Occupancy is from the hand-scored position labels (self in port, other in port), not from AlphaTracker distance.
20 sessions (main) or 34 files, against the paper's 31 sessions; the files count the two views of 14 sessions as separate pairs.

outcomes.statement: Relative dominants were more successful at displacing subordinates from the port, over the whole competition and during the tone.
outcomes.quote: Relative dominants were more successful displacing subordinates from the reward port throughout the competition
outcomes.notes: Over the 13 sessions where both mice's files are labelled and both pushed, dominants displaced the competitor in 91.7% of their pushes and subordinates in 60.2% over the labelled bins (mean difference 31.5 points, 95% CI 13.5 to 49.6, paired t-test p = 0.0051), and 93.4% against 56.5% during the tone (p = 0.0013).
deviations: "Whole competition" is the labelled bins (-2 to +12 s of each trial); the labels do not cover the intertrial intervals.
A push's outcome is in the competitor's file only, so the test uses 13 sessions with both files, against the paper's 32 and 31.

Pushing success as the Methods define it ("percent of pushing that resulted in displacing competitor"); a push is a run of push bins, successful when the competitor's file labels any of its bins displaced.

outcomes.statement: Total time being displaced from the port did not differ by relative rank in the recording cohort.
outcomes.quote: Total time being displaced from reward port by relative rank in dataset used for mPFC recordings (n=31 sessions; paired t-test p=0.15)
outcomes.notes: Time labelled displaced did not differ by relative rank over the 14 sessions with both files; dominants 3.21 s and subordinates 3.93 s (mean difference -0.71 s, 95% CI -2.19 to 0.76, paired t-test p = 0.359); during the tone 2.71 against 3.14 s (p = 0.512); unpaired over all 34 files 3.47 against 4.41 s (Welch p = 0.43).
deviations: 14 sessions, against the paper's 31; time is over the labelled bins only.

outcomes.notes: The units tables hold 5,879 Klusta clusters, every one labelled unsorted, where the paper analyses 998 manually curated cells (913 kept for clustering); no curation label is filled in, and no rule on firing rate comes near 998 (5,232 clusters at or above 0.05 Hz, 2,075 above 1 Hz). findings.statement: The spike_times of every units table are two thirds of the time of the same spikes in the ElectricalSeries. Multiplied by 1.5 they line up with threshold crossings of the recording (cross-correlation peaks of 14 to 95 SD in 50 of 53 files, none above 7 SD unscaled), and the last spike of every file falls at 0.63 to 0.68 of the recording length. The times look divided by 30 kHz where the logger samples at 20 kHz.

In 18 of the 21 mPFC-LH files and one ephys file the rescaled spike times match the ElectricalSeries only after an offset of 5 to 28 s, and in 3 mPFC-LH files (20191025-chrimson2-3-1v3, 20191029-chrimson1-1-1v2, 20191029-chrimson1-2-1v2) at no offset within 60 s, so in those files the sorted spikes and the raw recording do not share a start.

The offset between the neural recording and the behaviour clock of the tone times, port entries and labels is in no file, though the dandiset description says a video_gap variable holds it. Estimated from the units' responses to port entries it is 4 to 45 s, differing by session (294 s in one file), and it cannot be estimated for the 10 ephys files, which have no port entries, or for 12 of the 38 files with them. An analysis aligning spikes to the task can rely on the files alone only where the port entries give a clear offset (23 of the 34 labelled files).

Every one of the 5,879 Klusta clusters is labelled unsorted, where the paper analyses 998 manually curated cells. The quality column exists but no cluster carries a curation label, so the paper's cells cannot be told from multi-unit and noise clusters, and none of the single-unit findings can be tested.

The dandiset holds no alone sessions, no phototagging light pulses, no optogenetic experiments, no unimplanted cohort, no ex vivo recordings, no AlphaTracker evaluation frames, no body weights and no port location.
The 10 ephys files hold no port entries, labels or poses, and in all 22 mPFC-BLA files every pose value is missing; 17 of the 53 competitions have no labels of either mouse.
Poses are given for Mouse1 and Mouse2 with nothing saying which is the file's subject, and without the nose that the Methods say was tracked (ears, tail base and logger only).

Reward deliveries are 0.49 s after tone onset in every file, where the Methods give 2 s. The tone times are the program's schedule, the same in all files of a cohort (all 53 share the first 17 onsets), not times recorded per session; in 7 of the 10 ephys files the last tones fall after the end of the neural recording.
pair_in_dataset is 'not included' in all 53 files, but for 20 sessions the competitor's file is in the dandiset.

sub-20200121-BLA2-1-1v2 has a session start of 2020-01-22 13:30, while its labels mirror those of its competitor's file in the 2020-01-21 13:15 session; the subject description of sub-20200123-BLA1-3-2v3 names mouse 2 against mouse 3, where the file name says mouse 3 against mouse 2 (its ranks are those of the file name's mice).

The ElectricalSeries of sub-20191025-chrimson2-3-1v3 is the same signal as that of sub-20191029-chrimson2-3-1v3 (identical samples at three points, same length), while their units differ and the 20191025 file's units match its recording at no offset; the 20191025 file most likely carries the 20191029 recording in place of its own.

Where both mice of a session are labelled, one file's labels are the other's seen from the competitor (self and other in port swapped, a push opposite displaced or resist), in every bin for most sessions; in 20200121-BLA2-3v4 and 20200122-BLA1-3v4 only 76% and 68% of position bins agree.

The 34 labelled files hold 965 trials from 14 mice, the size of the paper's HMM-GLM dataset (965 trials, 32 sessions, 13 mice), and the 53 files hold the 53 competitions of ED Fig. 5b (12, 11, 15 and 15 per rank against 12, 12, 15 and 14).

In 18 of the 34 labelled files the labels hold fewer trials than the file has tones, and nothing says which tones were scored. Against the port entries, several files match only when the label trials start at a later tone (20200122-BLA2-1-1v4 at r = 0.76 from the third tone, against -0.02 from the first), and in others no start gives a clear match.

The paper's processed HMM-GLM input (Tyelab/HMMGLM) matches the dandiset's labelled trials (for the 512 trials used for the HMM-GLM, median label agreement with the best-matching trial 0.91, against 0.70 for the second best), and against it the spikes of all 34 labelled files peak at one offset, which agrees within 1 s with the port-entry offset in 20 of the 23 files where both are clear. So the missing video_gap can be recovered for the labelled files from the paper's own input; the files alone give it for 23.

The paper's processed HMM-GLM input holds 14 animals (trial2animal), where Methods 17 says 13 mice; its 965 trials and its rank per trial (487 dom, 478 sub) match the 34 labelled files of the dandiset, where the ED Fig. 5k legend gives 482 dom trials.

Methods 17 does not say in which direction the multi-unit threshold of 4 SD from the mean is applied, or whether the HMM-GLM input is counts or normalised rates. On the dandiset's recordings the two directions give different outcomes for ED Fig. 5k. Which did the paper use? Its processed input holds counts, matched trial by trial at 1.06 times the crossings in either direction and 1.47 times the negative crossings computed here.

The paper does not say how the reward latencies of ED Fig. 5d were matched to trials, nor which tones the hand-scored labels cover where a file has fewer label trials than tones. Were the latencies taken from the port entries (lickometer or beam) or from the scored video, and which tone does each label trial belong to?

entries.name: 001749-padilla-coreano-2022
entries.title: Social competition behaviour in the mPFC recording cohort (Padilla-Coreano et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Padilla-Coreano, Batra, Patarino et al. (2022) on dandiset 001749, which holds the wireless mPFC recordings of 20 mice in 53 reward competitions, with tone times, port entries, AlphaTracker poses and the nine hand-scored behaviour labels. It checks the files' clocks and units against the paper and tests the behavioural findings of Extended Data Fig. 5 (competitions won by rank, rewards, latency, port occupancy, pushing success and time displaced) and the HMM-GLM decoding of behaviour from multi-unit activity (Figure 1i, ED Fig. 5j-k), with the paper's HMM-GLM code ported from MATLAB, on the files whose neural offset can be placed. The single-unit findings cannot be tested, as the files do not mark the paper's curated cells.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Padilla-Coreano et al. (2022) from dandiset 001749
